title: Normalized exact integral-monodromy realization data
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A$ and chosen uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. A monodromy base consists of a connected qcqs scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying space is Noetherian, a geometric point $\bar t$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and a profinite model $G$ of its etale fundamental group, with its specified actions on the finite-etale fibre functor [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Use the existing category of jointly continuous finite-dimensional $E$-representations of $G$, with its spectral-norm module topology and equivariant linear maps [def-pod-l-adic-representations], [cor-galois-lisse-representations]. Use sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the continuous-function coefficient rings $A_T,E_T$ [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients] on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Lisse means locally free of finite, possibly zero and locally varying, rank.

An invariant lattice in $V$ is an actual stable finite free $A$-submodule $B\subset V$ whose $E$-span is $V$. Its positive-level quotient is $Q_n=B/\varpi^{n+1}B$ for $n\geq0$, with the canonical residue map. A lattice normalization of a functor $J$ consists of: a finite-coefficient correspondence $c$ of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1); a diagram $F:\mathbf N^{op}\to\operatorname{Sh}(T_{et},A)$ whose underlying set sheaves are finite locally constant; $A$-linear fibre isomorphisms $F_n{}_{\bar t}\cong Q_n$; and the requirements that every transition sends the residue of $b$ to the residue of $b$, and the fibre action under $c$ sends that residue to the residue of $gb$. Thus these are precisely the finite local systems associated to the quotient representations, including their maps. It also consists of an $A_T$-module $M_B$ with a limit cone identifying its underlying abelian sheaf with $\varprojlim_n\nu^*F_n$, where $\nu^*$ is the canonical comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Each projection respects every constant scalar $a\in A$. Finally it has an isomorphism $\eta_B:J(V)\cong E_T\otimes_{A_T}M_B$, with this scalar extension the sheafified change of rings [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

Compatibility on a lattice-preserving equivariant map $f:(V,B)\to(W,C)$ consists of a map $M_B\to M_C$ and a map of the finite diagrams whose fibre is the quotient of $f$ at every level. The integral map commutes with all limit projections, and its scalar extension commutes with $J(f)$ under the specified $\eta_B,\eta_C$.

A normalized exact monodromy realization is a functor $J:\operatorname{Rep}^{cont}_E(G)\to\operatorname{Mod}(E_T)$, together with the finite correspondence above, which is fully faithful, additive and respects multiplication by every $E$ scalar, has lisse values, and carries every representation sequence whose underlying vector-space maps are injective, exact in the middle and surjective to an ambient short exact sequence of sheaf modules. It includes normalizations simultaneously for every $V$ and every invariant lattice $B$, and compatible maps for every lattice-preserving equivariant map. Commensurability of lattices then gives the lattice-independent integral-monodromy realization followed by inversion of $\ell$.

source.place: Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4),(6), pp. 59–60, and the integral-monodromy reduction in the proof of Corollary 6.8.5, p. 60. The exact-realization formulation makes the comparison used in that proof explicit; it does not assert closure of all pro-étale lisse sheaves.
